clue.text: Kitchen sideboard wanted for theatre employee

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cabinet with shelves for crockery
second meaning: the backstage worker who helps actors into costume

explanation.surface: A theatre is advertising for staff, and a piece of kitchen furniture seems to be on the job list.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a piece of furniture with shelves for plates and the backstage helper who looks after an actor's costumes.

clue.text: Describes tea, say, in spiced mixture

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the jumbled word
a mixture is a blend, so the word before it has its letters mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: say tells the solver to use the sound of the word before it, not its spelling

parts.note: the drink sounds like the letter

explanation.surface: Someone explains what goes into a cup of spiced chai.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something is to portray or represent it in words or pictures, the same as describing it.

clue.text: Person in administration wanted about four put to death

indicators.note: about means around, so the following word is wrapped around the number

parts.note: to execute is to put to death
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A wanted official faces capital punishment along with three others.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior manager whose job is to run an organisation's administration.

clue.text: Charming little street on the outskirts

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so one piece stands on either side of the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A pretty little lane lies at the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet in the sense of delightful or appealing is a close synonym of charming.

clue.text: Videos court officials

definitions.meaning: first meaning: machines that tape television programmes
second meaning: judges in English courts of a certain rank

explanation.walkthrough: 'Videos' reads as a verb about filming the court; it is a noun for the machines. A recorder is also a part-time judge in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Video recorders are the machines people called videos, and recorders are also a rank of English judge.

clue.text: Contemplate getting into bed, bewildered!

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: taken as written; it is the outer piece
to muse is to ponder or contemplate

explanation.surface: Someone ponders climbing into bed and ends up confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused is a synonym for puzzled or confused, describing someone at a loss.

clue.text: Boring billboard's first to come down

indicators.note: first points to only the opening letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: just the first letter of this word
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A dull advertising hoarding is to be taken down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland means lacking interest or flavour, so it serves as a synonym for dull and boring.

clue.text: Manufacture women's garment as a temporary substitute

parts.note: to make is to manufacture
a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: Run up a dress quickly to serve as a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift is something improvised to serve for the time being until the proper thing is available.

clue.text: Person who is late starts silly quarrel

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter only of the word that follows

parts.note: just the first letter of this word
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone who arrives late sparks a pointless argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a corpse, and the late are those who have died.

clue.text: Leading doctor agreed being wrong causes dishonour

indicators.note: leading points to the first letter only of the following word

parts.note: just the first letter of this word

indicators.note: something wrong is not in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A senior doctor's mistaken agreement brings shame on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to humiliate or lower them in esteem, the verb sense of dishonour.

clue.text: Music in "Thieving Magpie" cellists love

parts.note: surface padding: completes the opera's title

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters are sitting inside the following words of the clue

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next
surface padding: finishes the sentence about the players

explanation.surface: Cellists are fond of Rossini's overture The Thieving Magpie.
explanation.walkthrough: PIECE spans magPIE CEllists; 'love' only finishes the surface sentence. The Thieving Magpie is itself a musical piece, an opera by Rossini.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single musical composition, so music in the sense of a work can be called one.

clue.text: Left in excellent bit of roast pork

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the word that follows

parts.note: cracking is informal British for excellent
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A cook praises the delicious crispy part of a pork roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling is the crisp, browned rind of roast pork, the crunchy part many diners prize.

clue.text: Opposed to having journalist behind bar

indicators.note: behind says the journalist comes after the bar in the finished word

parts.note: the counter is the bar in a pub or shop
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a reporter standing behind the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter an argument or move is to oppose it with one of your own.

clue.text: Where one is sitting in an upholstered seat?

indicators.note: sitting in something means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sofa is an upholstered seat for several people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a person sits on a padded couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' is the definition: the answer is a place, the capital of Bulgaria, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A city is a location, so a capital name can answer the question of where something is.

clue.text: Go round for something for her to wear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pass around the edge of something, avoiding it
second meaning: a garment hanging from the waist

explanation.surface: Someone is sent out to shop for a woman's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bypass or move along the edge of; the noun is a women's garment hanging from the waist.

clue.text: In a diplomatic way, filled in catty members

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the following word
a weak signal: the members of the word are taken and reassembled in another order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
something filled is full

explanation.surface: Spiteful people were informed of something with tact.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lacks a clear anagram signal for catty; 'members' is the only word left to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting tactfully means handling people with sensitivity and discretion, which is how a diplomat behaves.

clue.text: Get rid of brewed ale in time

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: Advice to finish off the beer that's being made before it's too late.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove it entirely, a direct synonym of discarding it.

clue.text: Fashionable because about to become hypocritical

parts.note: in means fashionable
since can mean because
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Following fashion purely for its own sake makes a person a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: An insincere person says what they do not mean, which is the core of being hypocritical.

clue.text: Excellent! Blair made changes

indicators.note: making changes means altering things, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: both words are used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Praise for the reforms of Tony Blair, the former British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirable means deserving praise and respect, close in sense to outstanding or excellent.

clue.text: Drills and cuts out round a ruler

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to excise is to cut something out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A routine of practice sessions and trimming done around a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercises are repeated practice routines, the same thing as military or school drills.

clue.text: Divorcee sat for an artist, naked

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
a model who sits for a painter poses

explanation.surface: A former wife modelled for a painter in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means uncovered and laid bare, so it fits naked in the sense of unclothed.

clue.text: Try to persuade relief worker to start talking

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker who relieves permanent staff

indicators.note: to start points to the opening letter only of the following word

parts.note: just the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Trying to coax a stand-in employee into opening up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or coax them into doing something.

clue.text: Handled in a patient way?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dealt with or managed
second meaning: given medical care, as a patient is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the adjective for calm; it is the noun, someone receiving medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dealt with in some manner and given medical attention, as happens to a patient.

clue.text: Poor misguided fellow needed evidence

indicators.note: something misguided has gone astray, so these letters are led into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A hapless man who got things wrong needs evidence to back him.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that establishes a fact, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Eye crooked cop with it

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a watchful eye on a corrupt police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an informal or jocular term for the eye, the organ of sight.

clue.text: Be taking on a bit of a French emperor

indicators.note: taking in something means holding it inside, so the first word wraps the rest

parts.note: taken as written; it is the outer piece
on and a are kept as written; a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Someone is told to play a small role as Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804; his surname identifies him.

clue.text: Unable to see, as closed at one end

definitions.meaning: second meaning: as in a dead-end alley

explanation.definitionFit: Blind means sightless, and a blind alley or tube is one with no exit at the far end.

clue.text: Spike, caught in an apron, goes red!

indicators.note: caught in says the letters are trapped inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next
surface padding: the blush that completes the picture

explanation.surface: Someone blushes after snagging an apron on a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: PRONG sits in aPRON Goes; 'an' and 'red' only complete the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a sharp pointed tine, as on a fork, so it is a kind of spike.

clue.text: Tease, till upset, a space traveller

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: both words are used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Keep teasing an astronaut until they get upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is an object orbiting the Earth, so it travels through space.

clue.text: Encircle the globe with it

parts.note: an orb is a sphere or globe
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to go all the way round the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'the globe' the thing circled; it is a separate piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit something is to travel in a circular path around it, which is to encircle it.

clue.text: Rotten month? Yes, to a former copper!

parts.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December
aye is an old or dialect word for yes
D stood for the old penny, a copper coin before British decimalisation in 1971

explanation.surface: Someone asks a retired policeman whether a month has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but here it is a coin: the pre-1971 British penny, abbreviated D.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed food or wood has decomposed, which is what it means to be rotten.

clue.text: Intellectual, for example, and good to lead

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
G is the abbreviation for good
to head a group is to lead it

explanation.surface: A clever person is held up as a fine model of leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is an informal, slightly mocking name for a bookish, highly intellectual person.
